original_question: How does the graph complex act on the space of deformation-quantisation star-products, especially under gauge transformations ⋆⇄⋆′, when the leading Poisson bi-vector in a Kontsevich star-product ⋆ = × + ħ{·,·}_P + o(ħ) is shifted by a graph-generated symmetry Q(P)=O→r(γ)(P) to P+εQ(P)+o(ε)? Can this action be described explicitly and illustrated by examples?
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at the paper’s unnumbered quantum-aspect open problem at the end of the note: to make explicit how Kontsevich’s graph complex acts on the space of Kontsevich deformation-quantization star-products, when a graph cocycle produces an infinitesimal Poisson symmetry of the leading bivector.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant part of the paper as a quantum/deformation-quantization question, not the combinatorial or Poisson-cohomology nontriviality questions. It correctly uses the Kontsevich star-product, the idea of an infinitesimal graph-generated deformation P ↦ P + εQ(P), and the role of gauge transformations between star-products. It also correctly asks for an explicit description of the induced action.
missing_details: The paper’s scope is finite-dimensional affine Poisson manifolds; your draft should state that ambient setting explicitly.
P should be specified as a Poisson bivector, i.e. [[P,P]] = 0.
γ should be specified as a graph cocycle in Kontsevich’s graph complex, not just an arbitrary graph expression.
Q(P) should be identified as the universal infinitesimal symmetry obtained from γ by the orientation morphism, so that P + εQ(P) is Poisson only to first order, modulo o(ε).
The star-product in question is specifically Kontsevich’s star-product attached to P, not an arbitrary deformation-quantization star-product.
The action being asked for should be clarified: is it on actual star-products, on gauge-equivalence classes of star-products, or on chosen gauge-related representatives star and star′?
If star′ is mentioned, the gauge transformation between star and star′ should be defined as the usual formal differential-operator equivalence in deformation quantization.
The formal nature of the parameters should be stated: ħ is the deformation parameter of the star-product, ε is an infinitesimal parameter for the graph flow.
The paper frames this as an open problem/question, not as an established construction with a worked-out answer.
The request for 'illustrated by examples' is natural, but it is not part of the nearest official formulation in the paper.
refined_question: Let P be a Poisson bivector on a finite-dimensional affine manifold, and let ⋆ = × + ħ{·,·}_P + o(ħ) be the Kontsevich star-product associated with P. If γ is a cocycle in Kontsevich’s graph complex and Q(P) = Or(γ)(P) is the corresponding universal infinitesimal symmetry of Poisson brackets, so that P_ε = P + εQ(P) + o(ε) is again Poisson to first order in ε, what is the induced action of γ on the associated Kontsevich star-product: explicitly, how does the star-product attached to P_ε relate to that attached to P, and how should this action be described on the space of Kontsevich star-products, modulo or in the presence of the usual gauge equivalences ⋆ ⇄ ⋆′?
justification: The draft is not trying to capture the paper’s main combinatorial questions about graph cocycles or its separate question about Poisson-cohomology nontriviality. Rather, it targets the note’s final quantum-aspect problem, signposted already in the abstract by the phrase 'quantum aspects of the theory' and then formulated in the closing discussion as the problem of understanding explicitly the action of the graph complex on Kontsevich star-products. The draft is already close because it uses the exact deformation-quantization setup the paper has in mind: a Kontsevich star-product whose leading term is controlled by a Poisson bivector, together with an infinitesimal graph-generated deformation of that bivector. What it still lacks is the paper’s ambient setting (finite-dimensional affine manifolds), the cocycle/orientation-morphism origin of Q(P), the first-order nature of the deformation P + εQ(P), and the precise distinction between star-products themselves and their gauge-equivalence classes. The paper presents this as an open problem rather than as a theorem or proposition, so no paper-certified equivalent reformulation is available.
